artikel.titel: France’s social demands run up against tightening fiscal constraints
artikel.text: EUROPE: Thursday’s nationwide mobilisation over wages and purchasing power will add pressure on a French government already struggling with weak growth, a fragile labour market and an increasingly unmanageable budget. Its options for responding to social discontent are narrowing as higher borrowing costs further weaken the outlook for public debt

artikel.titel: Uzbekistan rates stay on hold, but hopes for 2027 cuts remain
artikel.text: COMMONWEALTH OF INDEPENDENT STATES: The Central Bank of Uzbekistan kept its policy rate unchanged at 14.00%, as expected, but delivered a more hawkish message than in September. Higher inflation and GDP forecasts suggest that easing in 2026 is now less likely. But we still see scope for cuts in 2027, assuming continued fiscal restraint and potential FX strength

artikel.titel: Rates Outlook 2027: The Good, the Bad and the Ugly
artikel.text: The spaghetti-western title neatly captures the three big forces shaping long-end rates: the ‘good’ of AI-driven productivity, the ‘bad’ of elevated fiscal deficits, and the ‘ugly’ of renewed inflationary pressure from ongoing wars. By the middle of 2027, however, things should start to look a little less ugly as inflation falls

artikel.titel: The Good the Bad and the Ugly for Rates in 2027
artikel.text: The spaghetti-western title neatly captures the three big forces shaping long-end rates: the ‘good’ of AI-driven productivity, the ‘bad’ of elevated fiscal deficits, and the ‘ugly’ of renewed inflationary pressure from ongoing wars. By the middle of 2027, however, things should start to look a little less ugly as inflation falls

artikel.titel: US rates and a triple whammy of obstacles to overcome
artikel.text: The good (AI), the bad (deficits) and the ugly (inflation) extend well beyond the US, with similar dynamics at play in France, Japan and the UK. While our focus here is the US, many of the same themes apply elsewhere. We think it will prove tough to shake off these impulses through the end of 2026 and into the first quarter of 2027

artikel.titel: Euro rates have good reason to be nervous
artikel.text: EUROPE: Easing inflation fears should bring euro rates down by mid-2027, but the path lower will be bumpy. We shift our attention from oil to inflation data and expect markets to react anxiously to upside surprises. Rising bond issuance outside the US government and AI could catch markets by surprise, but that is not our base case

artikel.titel: European bond spreads in a duel with the ‘Bad’
artikel.text: EUROPE: Fiscal strains and election risks are putting eurozone bonds to the test. France is the key fault line, while Bunds’ safe-haven appeal masks mounting supply pressures. We see a turbulent first half of 2027, and any relief hinges on a credible path to French fiscal consolidation

artikel.titel: A delayed landing for GBP rates
artikel.text: EUROPE: GBP rates seem to have drifted too high versus Bank of England expectations, which we attribute to a significant risk premium stemming from prior trading trauma. We therefore see rates lower across the curve, but only once inflation risks settle and US rates ease lower. Meanwhile, structural supply factors will keep the sterling curve steeper

artikel.titel: The grand Dutch pension reform finale
artikel.text: EUROPE: The biggest wave of Dutch pension reform is still to come, with more than €900bn in assets set to transition in 2027. Yet we expect the immediate market impact to remain limited. Healthy funding ratios should contain large-scale hedge unwinds, while the more lasting consequence will be more frequent swap rebalancing as hedging becomes tied to asset prices

artikel.titel: Czech core inflation warrants a rate hike
artikel.text: CENTRAL AND EASTERN EUROPE: Headline inflation came in slightly below market expectations in October, but the core rate likely increased, highlighting its persistence. Fuel prices declined sharply due to government measures, yet may rebound in future. We see a rate hike as the likely outcome of tomorrow’s CNB vote. A disappointing GDP reading will put a lid on any hiking spree
